questions.text: Medical Practitioner Licensing: Verification of licenses: (1) Automated check with Medical Board (if API available); (2) Manual verification process; (3) License expiry tracking; (4) Disciplinary history check; (5) Scope of practice verification (e.g., nurse vs doctor); (6) Cross-border licensing (can doctor treat patient in another country?).
questions.evidence_required: Verification SOPs, License database, Expiry tracking logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Manual verification often needed (no APIs). Cross-border telemedicine common but legally grey. Scope of practice critical (nurses doing doctor work).

questions.text: Telemedicine Specific Regulations: Compliance with tele-health rules: (1) Telemedicine license (if required); (2) Prescription restrictions (e.g., no narcotics via video); (3) Patient consent for telemedicine; (4) Record keeping standards; (5) Emergency referral protocols; (6) Liability insurance for telemedicine.
questions.evidence_required: Telemedicine license, Consent forms, Prescription policy, Insurance certificate
questions.africa_specific_notes: Telemedicine guidelines emerging (Kenya, Nigeria, SA have them). Narcotics restrictions common. Liability insurance often overlooked.

questions.text: Pharmacy & Drug Regulation: Compliance for e-pharmacy: (1) Pharmacy Board registration; (2) Pharmacist supervision requirements; (3) Controlled substance handling; (4) Cold chain compliance certification; (5) Import licenses (if importing drugs); (6) Anti-counterfeit measures.
questions.evidence_required: Pharmacy licenses, Pharmacist contracts, Cold chain certs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Online pharmacy highly regulated. Pharmacist must supervise. Counterfeits are the main regulatory target.

questions.text: Health Data Protection Compliance: Compliance with DPA/GDPR: (1) Data Protection Officer (DPO) appointment; (2) Health data classification (sensitive personal data); (3) Data sovereignty (hosting in-country if required); (4) Breach notification protocol; (5) Processor agreements (with cloud providers); (6) Impact assessments (DPIA).
questions.evidence_required: DPO appointment letter, DPIA reports, Hosting contracts, Breach protocol
questions.africa_specific_notes: Health data is 'Sensitive Personal Data' in most African DPAs. Local hosting often mandated (e.g., Nigeria, Kenya for government data).

questions.text: Consent Management Governance: Governance of patient consent: (1) Explicit consent for data collection; (2) Consent for sharing (referrals, insurance); (3) Age of consent (minors accessing sexual health); (4) Withdrawal of consent mechanism; (5) Auditability of consent.
questions.evidence_required: Consent flows, Audit logs of consent
questions.africa_specific_notes: Minors accessing sexual health (HIV/contraception) is legally complex. Consent must be informed (literacy issues).

questions.text: Clinical Oversight Structure: Who is responsible for medical quality: (1) Chief Medical Officer (CMO) role; (2) Medical Advisory Board; (3) Clinical protocol review process; (4) Peer review of consultations; (5) Adverse event reporting system; (6) Quality improvement plans.
questions.evidence_required: Org chart (CMO), Committee minutes, Peer review logs, Adverse event reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Tech companies often lack medical leadership. CMO is essential. Peer review ensures doctors don't cut corners.

questions.text: Adverse Event Management: Handling medical errors: (1) Reporting mechanism for errors/near misses; (2) Investigation process (Root Cause Analysis); (3) Reporting to authorities (if required); (4) Patient disclosure policy; (5) Corrective action tracking.
questions.evidence_required: Incident logs, RCA reports, Corrective action plans
questions.africa_specific_notes: If a patient dies or is harmed, there must be a process. 'Move fast' doesn't apply to medical errors.

questions.text: Medical Ethics Compliance: Adherence to ethical principles: (1) Beneficence (act in patient interest); (2) Non-maleficence (do no harm); (3) Autonomy (patient choice); (4) Justice (fair access); (5) Conflict of interest policy (pharma kickbacks); (6) Research ethics (if using data for research).
questions.evidence_required: Code of Ethics, Conflict of interest declarations, IRB approvals (for research)
questions.africa_specific_notes: Pharma kickbacks are a major ethical risk. Research on African data requires IRB approval.

questions.text: Algorithmic Ethics (AI in Health): Governance of AI tools: (1) Bias testing (skin tone, gender); (2) Explainability requirements; (3) Human-in-the-loop for critical decisions; (4) Liability assignment (AI vs Doctor); (5) Validation on local datasets.
questions.evidence_required: Bias test reports, Validation studies, Liability policy
questions.africa_specific_notes: AI trained on Western data fails in Africa (e.g., skin lesions). Local validation mandatory.

scoring_notes: Layer 3 (Governance) for Healthcare in SSA: Medical licensing and data protection are the pillars. Clinical governance (CMO oversight) distinguishes legitimate health tech from dangerous apps.
